verification_note: All surviving findings re-verified against the worktree at 4677f83 (file reads + two headless scratch repros: ghost-pipe demolish bug reproduced; ADR-11 replay convention divergence reproduced). Post-review follow-up (owner ruling, houses don't connect to each other): added finding 47.

findings.title: NetworkHealth win/lose/drain has ZERO test coverage (P0 health/loss + the MVP win condition)
findings.evidence: run_tests.gd suite_paths lists test_parse_gate, test_catalogs, test_qos, test_demand, test_director, test_topology, test_routing, test_replay — no network_health suite anywhere in game/tests/.
findings.detail: The loss meter (Error 404) and the surge win condition (FR12) are the fun-test gate's terminal states; no regression test pins drain/grace/recharge/win/lose. Perkins scratch-verified the behavior works headless (lost at tick 250 no-build; won at surge end w/ network), but nothing in the suite guards it.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a test_network_health suite: meter drains on breach after grace, caps at max drain (E16), recharges on health, won/lost reachable, run_lost supersedes grace_expired (E17).

findings.title: QoS priority behavior (promote/demote, drop ladder, no-starvation) untested — only the WFQ partition helper is covered
findings.evidence: test_qos.gd contains only: _test_even_split_no_vanish, _test_default_weights_split, _test_all_zero_fallback, _test_zero_capacity — all static QoSEngine.allocate() calls. Nothing steps PacketFlow with a priority_class pipe.
findings.detail: The differentiator (FORGE #4) — a prioritized pipe promotes its class to Express and demotes the other to Best — has no behavioral test: no assert that streaming on a STREAM-priority pipe beats email under contention, no drop-ladder (E9) test, no no-starvation (E7) test.
findings.recommended_fix: Add flow-level tests: with a priority_class pipe, the promoted class's packets traverse/deliver under contention while the other drops first; assert lane ordering and the E9 ladder.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: FAIL
findings.evidence: tests lens per-chunk gates: chunk A FAIL (P0 gaps: NetworkHealth, QoS priority), chunk B CONCERNS (accumulator untested), chunk C FAIL (reported with A).
findings.detail: P0 <100% (NetworkHealth + QoS flow behavior + win/lose all uncovered); overall suite coverage of the fun-test loop's critical paths is below the gate threshold despite 62/62 green.
findings.recommended_fix: Close the two P0 gaps (blockers above); add the accumulator contract test (AC-E21) to lift the gate to PASS.

findings.title: Upgrade validation charges the full new-tier cost, but apply spends only the tier-delta
findings.evidence: _validate_upgrade: 'var cost: int = Economy.draw_cost(p.span_tiles, tier.cost_per_tile)' then '_apply_upgrade: economy.spend(maxi(0, new_cost - old_cost))'
findings.detail: Architecture §6.7: 'upgrade costs = length x tier; tier-delta for upgrades'. Validation demands the full new-tier price, so affordable delta upgrades are rejected unless the player holds the full cost. Budget is 3000 so it rarely binds, but the contract mismatch is real.
findings.recommended_fix: In _validate_upgrade, subtract the old tier's cost (like _apply_upgrade) before can_afford.

findings.title: Upgrade validation skips the span <= tier.max_span check that draw enforces
findings.evidence: _validate_upgrade checks missing_pipe / unknown_tier / over_budget only; no span_between <= tier.max_span test (contrast _validate_draw: 'if span > tier.max_span: rejected span_exceeds_tier').
findings.detail: A long pipe (e.g. span 16) can be upgraded to a tier whose max_span (standard=14) is smaller than the pipe's span, producing an over-span pipe the draw path forbids. UI cycles tiers upward only (narrow->standard->wide), so unreachable from the fun-test UI today.
findings.recommended_fix: Add the span check to _validate_upgrade: reject when p.span_tiles > tier.max_span.

findings.title: Junction demolish with parallel pipes leaves a ghost pipe referencing the removed node
findings.evidence: for nb in attached: 'var p: NetPipe = _pipe_between(dem.target_id, nb)' — _pipe_between returns ONE pipe per neighbor; with 2 parallel pipes content<->router, demolishing the router removed only 1 of 2. Scratch repro: pipes 3 -> 1 (expect 0), 'GHOST PIPE id=2 a=1 b=6' (b = demolished router).
findings.detail: The cascade removes one pipe per adjacent node; parallel pipes (E1.5) to the same neighbor survive as ghosts referencing a dead node id. Violates E11/E18 spirit (demolish cascades fully); in-flight packets on the ghost still traverse (benign), but the topology references a removed entity.
findings.recommended_fix: In _apply_demolish, iterate the pipes-by-pair groups and remove ALL pipes between the node and each neighbor (or reuse _remove_pipe per connected pipe id).

findings.title: balance.json logic_hz=10 contradicts ADR-2's 20Hz, the file's own comment, and CoreConst.DEFAULT_LOGIC_HZ — surge timings run ~2x the documented values
findings.evidence: balance.json: '"logic_hz": 10' with '_comment: ...logic_hz=20 -> 50ms/tick (ADR-2)'; demand.json comment: 'The Surge = streaming x10 for ~90s with a 30s forecast lead' — at 10Hz the surge is 1800 ticks = 180s with 60s lead.
findings.detail: ADR-2 pins LOGIC_HZ=20 (tunable in data, but the shipped value silently contradicts every comment + the ADR default). The surge the player faces is ~2x longer than designed. Determinism is unaffected (config choice), but the tuning spec is inconsistent.
findings.recommended_fix: Pick 20Hz (match ADR-2 + comments) or 10Hz (update CoreConst comment, balance/demand comments, and the surge duration language) — make data + comments agree.

findings.title: RunState.bootstrap never passes balance to PacketFlow — ms_per_tick stays 50 (balance says 10Hz -> 100ms), doubling latency accrual; balance lane weights never consulted
findings.evidence: 's.flow = PacketFlow.new(p_catalogs)' — no balance arg. PacketFlow._init: 'if balance != null and balance.logic_hz > 0: ms_per_tick = 1000 / balance.logic_hz' — balance null -> ms_per_tick = 50.
findings.detail: Every in-flight packet accrues 50ms/tick instead of 100ms (10Hz). Latency is recorded but not yet enforced (no latency-tol drops), so impact is latent — but the SLA data the spine produces is wrong by 2x, and _pipe_lane_caps silently falls back to compiled defaults.
findings.recommended_fix: Pass p_balance into PacketFlow.new(p_catalogs, p_balance) in bootstrap.

findings.title: Determinism fingerprint omits in-flight packet state and latency — AC-E10 replay-equality can pass while packet internals diverge
findings.evidence: to_fingerprint() covers tick/era/health/counts/sla{delivered,dropped,demand,uptime}/topology — no packet routes/progress/lane/accrued_latency; sla_summary omits total_latency_ms; 'util': n.utilization_units is always 0 (never updated anywhere).
findings.detail: Two runs with identical fingerprints could carry different in-flight packet internals (route/position/latency) — divergence only surfaces later, if at all. The keystone determinism test can't see the sim's most dynamic state.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend sla_summary with latency and include a compact packet-state hash (or per-class in-flight counts by edge) in the fingerprint.

findings.title: Replay-equality keystone (AC-E10) runs on a no-pipes topology — routing/traversal/QoS determinism never exercised
findings.evidence: _test_replay_equality: '_step_n(a, 40)' with '_step_n' passing '[]' as cmds every tick; bootstrap map has zero pipes; comment: 'empty action log'. _test_seed_changes_stream also steps no-pipe runs and compares rng.state.
findings.detail: The test proves seeded spawn-stream determinism only. Commands, routing, bandwidth traversal, and QoS lane behavior — the state-affecting paths ADR-10 cares about — are never re-stepped. Perkins' scratch: a command-driven replay reproduces byte-identically with the +1 convention, but the suite doesn't pin it.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a replay test that draws pipes + sets a priority, steps both runs, and compares fingerprints; also re-step with the same action_log twice.

findings.title: submit_command applies edits immediately while SimDriver.step applies batches at tick start — ADR-11 action-log replay needs an undocumented +1 convention (naive replay diverges)
findings.evidence: submit_command: 'var r: EditResult = state.topology.apply_all([cmd]); if r.ok: state.action_log.append(cmd)' — applied between ticks with cmd.tick = _logic_tick. SimDriver.step: 'var apply_result: EditResult = state.topology.apply_all(cmds)' at the START of the tick.
findings.detail: A command tagged tick T is live-applied AFTER T's step (its flow). Replaying the log through step(T, [cmd]) applies it BEFORE T's flow — divergence (Perkins repro: first divergent tick = T). The matching convention (log cmd -> step T+1) is nowhere documented, enforced, or tested.
findings.recommended_fix: Document + test the convention: log entries apply at the start of the NEXT tick after their recorded tick; add a live-vs-replay regression test with commands.

findings.title: AC-E21 slow-mo contract violated: accumulator cap discards backlog (skips ticks) and no 'can't keep up' telemetry is emitted
findings.evidence: 'if accumulator > tick_len * float(MAX_STEPS_PER_FRAME): accumulator = tick_len * float(MAX_STEPS_PER_FRAME)' — excess time is dropped; comment claims 'the sim simply runs slow — AC-E21: never skips ticks'.
findings.detail: Under sustained overload the backlog beyond 0.5s is discarded, so sim ticks are skipped and real-time parity is lost — the opposite of AC-E21's 'slow-mo, never skip, telemetry'. Sim is cheap today so it rarely engages, but the pinned contract is violated as written.
findings.recommended_fix: Replace the cap with a slow-mo policy: run behind (never discard), emit a 'can't keep up' counter/telemetry, or explicitly re-scope AC-E21 for the prototype.

findings.title: Onboarding-dismiss input is never consumed — the same click starts a phantom drag (can draw an unintended pipe) and SPACE dismiss re-pauses
findings.evidence: hud._unhandled_input dismiss branch: '_show_onboard = false; controller.set_paused(false); queue_redraw(); return' — no set_input_as_handled()/accept_event() anywhere in scripts/run/. RunView then receives the same event: left-click over a node starts _drag_active; release over another node submits a DrawPipeCmd; KEY_SPACE calls controller.toggle_pause().
findings.detail: First-run experience: dismissing the briefing by clicking a node can draw a pipe the player didn't intend; dismissing with SPACE unpauses then immediately re-pauses. Both verified by reading the event flow; two lenses agreed.
findings.recommended_fix: Call set_input_as_handled() (or accept_event()) in the HUD's dismiss branch before returning.

findings.title: Demolish-in-transit reroute / 'severance' drop (AC-E1) untested
findings.evidence: _handle_severed exists (reroute from current node, else drop 'severance') but no test in game/tests/ references severance, reroute, or demolish-with-traffic.
findings.detail: E1 is a pinned edge contract (reroute or severance drop, atomic per edge). Perkins scratch-verified the basic path works (no crash; clean drops), but the reroute-with-alternative-path branch is unverified.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a test: in-flight packets on a demolished pipe reroute when an alt path exists; drop with 'severance' when none.

findings.title: SLA uptime aggregation (overall/recent/class) untested — it feeds the untested NetworkHealth breach input
findings.evidence: No test file references overall_uptime_pct, recent_overall_uptime_pct, recent_class_uptime, or _push_rolling; the rolling window's -1 (neutral) semantics are unasserted.
findings.detail: The health meter's breach decision (the loss loop) depends entirely on these aggregations, including the zero-demand neutral path (E24). Untested means a wrong drain/recharge decision would pass CI.
findings.recommended_fix: Add SLA aggregation tests: mixing classes, zero-demand neutrality (E24), rolling-window slide.

findings.title: node_health_states (the 🟡/🔴 warning surface) untested
findings.evidence: node_health_states() — '🔴 is always traceable to a MEASURED load (never a phantom)' — has no test in game/tests/.
findings.detail: The crisis-fairness warning surface (strained -> critical) is the player's only predictability tool; the thresholds (70/90) and the never-phantom guarantee are unasserted.
findings.recommended_fix: Add tests: load below strain -> HEALTHY; above strain -> STRAINED; above critical -> CRITICAL; zero-throughput node -> HEALTHY.

findings.title: RunController fixed-timestep accumulator (AC-E21 clamp + slow-mo) has no test — an explicitly pinned headless contract
findings.evidence: No test in game/tests/ exercises the accumulator: catch-up stepping, MAX_STEPS_PER_FRAME cap, delta clamp (minf(delta, 0.25)), pause freezing.
findings.detail: The tick driver is the presentation/core boundary; its clamping and catch-up are pinned contracts (project-context [FinLT] trap + AC-E21). A regression here silently breaks determinism timing.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a headless test driving _process with synthetic deltas: catch-up steps, cap behavior, clamp, pause freeze.

findings.title: CrisisEngine S4 warning/crisis contracts (WarningSign lead times, CrisisEvent root_cause) are stubbed out
findings.evidence: evaluate(): 'report.forecast = director.forecast_for_era(era_id, tick)' then '# E4.1-E4.3 (S4): compute strain metrics, raise WarningSigns, fire fair crises...' — comment only, no implementation.
findings.detail: The surge IS delivered (scripted set-piece + forecast) and the 🟡/🔴 surface IS live (node_health_states), so the fun-test loop closes. The archetype-firing CrisisEngine is deferred — foundation-audit owns it. Not a blocker per the prototype lens-guard (stubbed system).
findings.recommended_fix: Leave for the foundation-audit; track E4.1-E4.3 explicitly as deferred debt.

findings.title: Packet pool-exhaustion drop (AC-E22) not enforced — IN_FLIGHT_CAP declared but unused
findings.evidence: const IN_FLIGHT_CAP: int = 6000 — never read; packets array grows unbounded (practically bounded by per-lane QUEUE_DROP_DEPTH=20 x 3 lanes x pipes).
findings.detail: E22's 'drop lowest-priority-lane first on exhaustion' is unimplemented; reachable cap is far below 6000 so no live impact.
findings.recommended_fix: Note for the foundation-audit; either enforce or delete the constant.

findings.title: Node strain/critical lead-time tunables are loaded but never applied
findings.evidence: balance.strain_lead_ticks (600) / critical_lead_ticks (200) load from JSON; node_health_states uses instantaneous load only — lead times never consulted.
findings.detail: The warning surface is instantaneous, not lead-time-smoothed; E3.3's 'strained -> critical with lead' nuance is deferred. Fun-test still shows the surface.
findings.recommended_fix: Foundation-audit: apply lead-time windows or drop the tunables.

findings.title: span_between uses float sqrt for a state-affecting value (ADR-10 letter deviation)
findings.evidence: 'return int(round(sqrt(float(dx * dx + dy * dy))))' — a single correctly-rounded IEEE-754 sqrt on small ints; code comment documents the reasoning.
findings.detail: ADR-10 says integer/fixed-point for state-affecting paths. Single-sqrt is bit-identical across ARM/x86 (correctly-rounded op), so risk is theoretical; worth a foundation-audit glance.
findings.recommended_fix: Document as an accepted deviation or replace with integer distance.

findings.title: Core typed to concrete ScriptedDirector instead of the CrisisDirector base (ADR-7 seam)
findings.evidence: RunState 'var director: ScriptedDirector' and CrisisEngine.evaluate(..., director: ScriptedDirector); the base CrisisDirector exists and ScriptedDirector extends it.
findings.detail: Architecture §10.4 explicitly sanctions MVP wiring ('the seam earns its place for the production rebuild, not in throwaway MVP code'), so this is a known, spec-accepted deviation.
findings.recommended_fix: Foundation-audit / E11: retype consumers to the base CrisisDirector.

findings.title: QoS priority-emphasis preset is a hardcoded literal, not catalog data
findings.evidence: 'if pipe.priority_class == &"streaming" or pipe.priority_class == &"email": weights = Vector3i(4, 1, 1)'
findings.detail: project-context 'numbers single-source': tunables belong in game/data/. The (4,1,1) emphasis preset is a balance number in code.
findings.recommended_fix: Move the priority-emphasis preset into balance.json and load it.

findings.title: clean_span default reads pt.max_span before max_span is loaded
findings.evidence: 'pt.clean_span = int(d.get("clean_span", pt.max_span))' precedes 'pt.max_span = int(d.get("max_span", 0))' — the fallback reads the field default (0), not the loaded value.
findings.detail: All catalog tiers set clean_span explicitly, so no live impact; a future entry omitting clean_span would silently get 0.
findings.recommended_fix: Reorder: load max_span first, then clean_span.

findings.title: _validate_set_weights documents a never-drop-class zero-lane guard (E6) that is absent
findings.evidence: Comment: 'a lane carrying a never-drop class may not be zeroed... validated here against the catalog's loss_tol=None types' — code only rejects negative weights.
findings.detail: E6's guard is documented but unimplemented. MVP has no loss_tol=None class (email 30%, streaming 10% are droppable), so no live impact.
findings.recommended_fix: Foundation-audit: implement the E6 guard when a never-drop class ships.

findings.title: _pick_dst accepts a mode argument it never uses
findings.evidence: 'static func _pick_dst(sinks, weights, src_id, mode: int, rng)' — the mode param is never read in the body (comment explains ROUND_ROBIN is 'designer mode, NOT the MVP default').
findings.detail: Dead parameter; the comment covers intent. Trivial.
findings.recommended_fix: Drop the param or implement ROUND_ROBIN properly.

findings.title: Surge-window accumulators are never reset between surges
findings.evidence: surge_delivered/surge_dropped accumulate while in_surge; reset_window() is defined but never called anywhere.
findings.detail: A second surge would double-count the first's traffic in the win check. The MVP catalog has exactly one surge and the run is terminal at its end (win or meter loss), so latent only.
findings.recommended_fix: Call reset_window() at surge end (or when the win check runs).

findings.title: QUEUE_DROP_DEPTH comment says oldest drops, but code drops the newest (tail)
findings.evidence: Const comment: 'per-pipe FIFO backlog before oldest drops'; code: 'idx_in_lane += 1; if idx_in_lane > QUEUE_DROP_DEPTH: _drop(...)' — the 21st+ packet in the lane's iteration (newest) is dropped each tick.
findings.detail: Behavior is a bounded-depth queue that sheds new arrivals; the doc claims FIFO oldest-first. Behavior is defensible; the comment lies.
findings.recommended_fix: Fix the comment to describe the depth-limit semantics.

findings.title: Multi-command batch can drive the budget negative: apply_all validates each cmd against the un-mutated budget and spend() has no floor
findings.evidence: apply_all: phase-1 validates every cmd against the same budget, phase-2 applies all with 'economy.spend(cost)' (no clamp). Two draws each affordable alone but not together both pass and overdraw.
findings.detail: E23's validate-all-then-apply validates against pre-batch state; cumulative cost isn't checked. UI submits single commands (submit_command), so unreachable from play.
findings.recommended_fix: Either check cumulative cost in apply_all or clamp spend at 0.

findings.title: Batch apply dereferences entities with no null guard — a batch targeting a just-removed entity crashes
findings.evidence: Apply phase uses direct _pipes[]/_nodes[] indexing ('var p: NetPipe = _pipes[up.pipe_id]'). A batch like [DemolishPipe(p), UpgradePipe(p)] passes validation (both valid pre-batch) then KeyErrors in apply.
findings.detail: Reachable only via the core API with adversarial batches; the UI and demo use single commands.
findings.recommended_fix: Re-validate during apply (or snapshot-validate with a mutation plan).

findings.title: ScriptedDirector._load uses the FileAccess.open() result with no null check
findings.evidence: 'var f := FileAccess.open(path, FileAccess.READ); var text := f.get_as_text()' — no null guard (catalogs._read_json guards the same call).
findings.detail: file_exists + open race/permission failure would crash on get_as_text(). Prototype-robustness nit.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a null check mirroring catalogs._read_json.

findings.title: NetworkHealth.update derefs balance unconditionally though _init tolerates a null balance
findings.evidence: _init: 'if balance != null: meter_pct = balance.meter_start_pct...' guards; update() uses balance.win_uptime_pct / meter_drain_per_tick_max / meter_recharge_per_tick with no guard.
findings.detail: Balance is always injected in practice (RunState.bootstrap), so no live path hits it.
findings.recommended_fix: Guard or document the invariant.

findings.title: MCPRuntime autoload enabled unconditionally — unauthenticated TCP control server on all interfaces, no debug gate
findings.evidence: project.godot: 'MCPRuntime="*uid://1nrmjgkqqhm0"' as an autoload; the addon starts 'server starting on port 7777' at _ready (observed in every headless run).
findings.detail: A release build would ship a control server with no auth. Dev convenience per the briefing (MCP-verified screenshots), but the production rebuild must gate or remove it.
findings.recommended_fix: Foundation-audit/E11: exclude the addon from release exports or gate on OS.is_debug_build().

findings.title: project.godot lost the orientation=0 (landscape) pin mandated by project-context
findings.evidence: [display] has viewport 1280x720, canvas_items/expand — but no window/handheld/orientation key; project-context: 'display/window/handheld/orientation=0 (SCREEN_LANDSCAPE — landscape-only)'.
findings.detail: On mobile the game could launch in portrait. Desktop fun-test unaffected. project-context says project.godot changes are design decisions, not drive-bys.
findings.recommended_fix: Restore display/window/handheld/orientation=0.

findings.title: _process catch-up loop keeps stepping after the run goes terminal
findings.evidence: _do_step sets 'paused = true' on terminal, but the while loop ('while accumulator >= tick_len and steps < MAX_STEPS_PER_FRAME: _do_step()') doesn't re-check paused — up to 4 extra steps in the same frame.
findings.detail: A handful of post-terminal ticks emit snapshots after run_ended; the View switches on run_ended so they're ignored. Cosmetic.
findings.recommended_fix: Check paused in the loop condition.

findings.title: _snapshot_now passes the live sim RNG into plan_pressure on the per-edit display path (latent ADR-9 break)
findings.evidence: 'director.plan_pressure(state.topology.snapshot(), state.era.era_id, _logic_tick, state.rng)' — the MVP ScriptedDirector ignores rng, so no consumption today.
findings.detail: A future director that consumes rng on this display path would perturb the sim's rng stream (ADR-9: all sim randomness from the one seeded generator, consumed identically).
findings.recommended_fix: Pass a scratch rng or null; document the no-consumption invariant.

findings.title: Demo network build ignores apply_edit results; failures leave a partial map silently
findings.evidence: Six sequential 'state.topology.apply_edit(...)' calls, no result checks; a budget/span rejection silently yields a partial network.
findings.detail: Demo/capture mode only (default budget 3000 and wide spans fit), so currently benign.
findings.recommended_fix: Check results and log failures in demo mode.

findings.title: --capture enables RunView capture but not RunController demo_mode — a capture run without --demo screenshots an empty map
findings.evidence: RunView: 'if a == "demo" or a == "capture": _capture_mode = true'; RunController: 'if _has_arg("demo"): demo_mode = true'. The two flags are independent.
findings.detail: The capture rig's screenshots show the demo network only when BOTH flags are passed; --capture alone produces pipe-less captures. The minion's screenshots used both, so the artifacts are fine.
findings.recommended_fix: Make --capture imply demo_mode (or document the flag pair).

findings.title: _draw_ellipse is defined but never called; play_w/play_h are computed but unused (scale math repeats the literals)
findings.evidence: func _draw_ellipse(...) has zero callers; 'var play_w: float = 1000.0 / var play_h: float = 600.0' are never read — _fit_view_to_nodes repeats its own literals.
findings.detail: Dead code + duplicated magic numbers in the view. Harmless.
findings.recommended_fix: Delete _draw_ellipse; derive the play area once.

findings.title: Bundle capsule is drawn over the pipe priority marker at the midpoint
findings.evidence: _draw order: _draw_pipes() then _draw_bundles(); parallel-pipe capsules render after the priority marker (drawn at the offset midpoint in _draw_pipes).
findings.detail: On the demo's 2-pipe content->router pair with a priority pipe, the LAG capsule can cover the STREAM PRIORITY label. Cosmetic.
findings.recommended_fix: Draw markers after bundles (or skip the marker inside the capsule).

findings.title: queue_command / _cmd_queue is a legacy path with no caller
findings.evidence: grep: queue_command appears only in its own definition; _cmd_queue is read in _do_step (always empty — submit_command bypasses it) and cleared in boot.
findings.detail: Dead legacy path; all commands flow through submit_command.
findings.recommended_fix: Delete or keep as documented API — no behavior impact.

findings.title: main.tscn + main.gd are orphaned placeholder scaffold, superseded by run.tscn as the boot scene
findings.evidence: project.godot: 'run/main_scene="res://scenes/run.tscn"'; scenes/ still contains main.tscn and scripts/main.gd (stale description text: 'the routing prototype build is to come').
findings.detail: Leftover scaffold from the pre-prototype repo; harmless but stale.
findings.recommended_fix: Delete the orphan scene/script or update the description.

findings.title: test_topology comment says narrow.max_span 8, but the catalog max_span is 10
findings.evidence: Comment: '(id 2 (span 40 >> narrow.max_span 8)' — catalog: narrow max_span 10. Test still passes (40 > 10).
findings.detail: Stale comment; the assertion is on the rejection, not the bound.
findings.recommended_fix: Update the comment to 10.

findings.title: Catalog load is happy-path-only — missing/invalid-JSON error paths and balance fallback untested
findings.evidence: test_catalogs covers load_default success, MVP types, int recast; no test feeds a missing file or invalid JSON to assert load_errors/has_errors or the BalanceData fallback.
findings.detail: The error surface exists ('errors are logged + surfaced (never swallowed)') but is unverified; a broken catalog file would fail loudly but untested.
findings.recommended_fix: Add error-path tests (missing file, invalid JSON -> load_errors populated, balance fallback).

findings.title: Content-host throughput hardcoded (40) in the bootstrap map diverges from the node_types catalog (80)
findings.evidence: 's.topology.spawn_node(..., CoreConst.TerminalRole.CONTENT_HOST, Vector2i(30, 14), 40, 0)' vs data/node_types.json 'content_host ... "throughput_units": 80'. Router 60 and residential 5 match their catalog rows.
findings.detail: Numbers-single-source violation: the content node's load surface (🟡/🔴) is driven by a literal (40) that disagrees with the catalog (80) — during the surge the content host reads CRITICAL at 64 u/s load even when the network is healthy. Either tuning is fine, but the duplication is the trap.
findings.recommended_fix: Spawn from the node_types catalog (or move the map's overrides into data).

findings.title: latency_tol_ms / max_loss_pct are loaded but never enforced; packet_flow header claims latency-tol drops that don't exist
findings.evidence: Header: 'DROP (latency_tol exceeded -> SLA loss; or unreachable -> visible unmet demand, E1.4)'; drop paths in _advance: queue_overflow / unreachable / severance only. latency_tol_ms and max_loss_pct have zero consumers (grep).
findings.detail: The latency dimension of the QoS model is inert: packets never drop on latency, per-class loss tolerances are decorative. Fine for the fun-test (contention drops carry the loop), but the header documents behavior that doesn't exist, and SLA latency data is already 2x off (see warning above).
findings.recommended_fix: Either implement latency-tol drops, or fix the header + flag latency as deferred for the foundation-audit.

findings.title: Terminal-to-terminal pipes are legal — houses can be connected directly to each other, bypassing the router (design ruling: locations attach to the network, never to each other)
findings.evidence: _validate_draw rejects self_loop / missing_node / unknown_tier / span_exceeds_tier / over_budget only — no node-kind check; NetNode.is_terminal() exists but draw never consults it. Geometry permits it: res(8,5)-res(8,14) = 9 tiles <= narrow.max_span 10. BFS (_node_path) then routes residential->residential email (the MVP demand pair) through the direct house pipe in 1 hop, bypassing the router.
findings.detail: Design ruling (game owner): houses don't connect to each other — a network-engineer game where locations attach to the network (junctions) only. The code allows house-to-house draws and the router is bypassable; the rule is also unwritten in the GDD/architecture edge contracts. Doesn't break the fun-test loop (demo + sensible play route through the router) but the topology model is unenforced.
findings.recommended_fix: Reject DrawPipeCmd when both endpoints are terminals (EditResult.rejected(&"terminal_to_terminal")) and pin the rule as a new edge contract + regression test.
